entry.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China (3 minute read)

entry.title: AST SpaceMobile is building its own reusable rocket, Blacklift, to launch its BlueBird satellites (2 minute read)
entry.content:
AST is building Blacklift, a 20-ton, three-stage rocket with two reusable lower stages, to launch up to five stacked BlueBirds per flight from late 2028. It sized the vehicle around its own constellation after launch delays, including a New Glenn failure, slowed deployment, though it keeps outside launch deals for 100+ satellites. The engines come from Firefly: 27 Miranda and 9 Vira for the first three rockets, plus a license to build them itself, in a deal valued above $1.3 billion.

entry.title: Yangwang's U9 Xtreme hits 503 km/h (312.65 mph), a one-way record, on tuned rear-wing angle, damping, and tire pressure (2 minute read)
entry.content:

After early runs topped out near 490 km/h, engineers adjusted rear-wing angle, rebound damping in the suspension software, and tire pressures.

entry.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Gen 2 cuts internal cabling 81% and swaps a swerve drive in about an hour (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Using data from 100,000+ operating hours, Boston Dynamics redesigned its trailer-unloading robot around downtime. It cut internal cabling 81% (about half a mile of wire), switched to automotive-grade connectors, and added continuous-rotation joints that no longer hit hard stops. A full swerve drive swap drops from a day to about an hour. It unloads up to 1,000 cases per hour (varies with weight and stacking) and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.

entry.title: Physicists used electrical noise to show electrons in a high-temperature superconductor pair up earlier than expected (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Superconductors carry current when electrons team up in pairs, but in cuprates (compounds containing copper in an anionic state), scientists couldn't tell if the pairs form early or just don't exist until the material gets cold enough. The team measured electrical noise, which gets louder when charge moves in pairs, and found the extra noise appearing early. That suggests the pairs are already there and are just failing to move together, which could be what limits how warm cuprates can superconduct.

entry.title: TSMC denies reports that it is planning 3D DRAM for Nvidia (2 minute read)
entry.content:
The Information reported that TSMC began planning 3D DRAM production, possibly by converting an existing fab, to give Nvidia a fourth memory source, but TSMC says it stays a pure-play logic foundry with no plans to make commodity memory. The engineering case against it is that 3D DRAM, which stacks memory cells vertically, is years out even for Micron, whose roadmap has at least four more planar nodes first, and TSMC has no competitive planar DRAM process to build on.

entry.title: FLIP software subtracts starlight in JWST coronagraph data with up to 15x better sensitivity (3 minute read)
entry.content:
A Northwestern-led team built FLIP, which makes a physics-based digital twin of the telescope's optics and adjusts it until it reproduces the observed starlight, then subtracts that simulated glare. On existing NIRCam data at 4.3 microns, it improved sensitivity up to 15x over the conventional KLIP method and recovered the giant planet 51 Eridani b, which standard processing couldn't separate from residual glare.

entry.title: LumiTac is a camera-free six-axis tactile sensor, 12 mm wide and about $7 in parts (2 minute read)
entry.content:
LumiTac pairs five photoemitters with five RGBW photoreceivers on opposing circuit boards joined by translucent silicone, so load-driven motion between the layers shifts the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The head is 12 mm across, 4.75 mm thick, under 2 g, and made with about $7 in components. Independent testing gave R² of 0.966 to 0.994, with mean absolute errors of 0.054 to 0.190 N in force and 0.304 to 1.419 mN·m in moment.

entry.title: SLAC confirms altermagnetism in manganese telluride with polarized X-rays, a magnet type aimed at spintronic memory (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Altermagnets are a third kind of magnet alongside ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Like antiferromagnets, they have no net magnetization, so stray fields can't flip them, but they can still carry spin-polarized currents, so their data can be read out. A SLAC-lead team shot polarized X-rays at maganese telluride and saw a directional signal that a conventional antiferromagnet can't produce. This work, published in Science, targets a usecase within spintronic memory.

entry.title: Eclypsium shows AI model weights can be altered in memory after integrity checks pass (3 minute read)
entry.content:

Attack paths run through host firmware, management controllers, and DPUs, and the report says Nvidia, AMD, Intel, and Arm systems are all exposed. Its fix is DPUs that enforce security policy independently of the AI system, plus full component inventories.

entry.content:
A theory paper proposes reading an Andreev qubit without ancilla qubits: its state shows up as an oscillating supercurrent in a large superconducting loop, and a small coil coupled to a SQUID picks up the magnetic signal. The method still disturbs the qubit, but within standard error-correction thresholds. It's a proposal in Physical Review B, supported by FAPESP, with no experiment yet.
